applicability.notes: A001 correctly binds M003 to V=ℝ, a=−R, b=R, f(r)=g(iota(y,r)), f'(r)=∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)), for arbitrary y. ℝ is complete; smoothness gives the derivative at every closed-interval point, including endpoints, and continuity on the compact interval gives interval integrability. Endpoints lie outside C for every y, hence both values are zero. A002 correctly binds M002 to the restricted Lebesgue measures on Qrest and [−R,R], scalar codomain ℝ and f(y,r)=∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)). These are finite, hence s-finite measures; f is continuous and bounded on their compact support, hence product integrable. The coordinate-product identification is justified in S003 and BG004. The supplied M signatures impose no additional unmet premise for these real-valued instances. No E application occurs.

argument.notes: At t0>0, N002 applies because t0 lies in int[t0/2,3t0/2]. The product rule gives exactly the two desired summands, up to symmetry of the real Euclidean dot product. Each line integral of the product derivative vanishes by M003. Product integration by M002 therefore makes its box integral zero; support in C⊂Q identifies this with the whole-space integral. Linearity for the two absolutely integrable summands gives N004 with the stated minus sign. No differentiation under an integral or unsupported limiting exchange occurs, and n=1 is explicitly included.

background_notes.fact: For jointly smooth u at fixed t0>0 and 1≤j≤n, g(x)=u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0) is smooth and ∂_{x_j}g=(∂_{x_j}u_t)·∂_{x_j}u+u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u.

grounds.reason: Joint smoothness provides all component derivatives and their continuity at positive times.
Derivatives and the dot product have the componentwise Euclidean meanings.

background_notes.justification: Expand the dot product into its finite sum of component products and apply the scalar product rule to each. Smoothness is preserved by derivatives, products and finite sums, giving the displayed identity and continuity of the derivative.

background_notes.fact: If a compact C lies in (−R,R)^n with R>0, there is an open neighborhood of the boundary of Q=[−R,R]^n disjoint from C. A function vanishing outside C therefore vanishes near that boundary; all points with j-th coordinate ±R lie outside C, even if other coordinates lie outside Q.

grounds.reason: C is compact, C⊂(−R,R)^n, R>0, and positive-order derivatives vanish outside C at t0∈int J.
g is a product containing those vanishing derivatives.

background_notes.justification: For nonempty C, the continuous positive function x↦min_{1≤k≤n}(R−|x_k|) has a positive minimum on C. A collar narrower than this minimum misses C. For empty C any collar works. The endpoint assertion follows directly from strict coordinate inequalities on C and is valid for every remaining-coordinate vector.

background_notes.fact: A continuous real function on a compact interval is bounded, measurable and absolutely Lebesgue integrable there. For a<b its oriented interval integral equals the Lebesgue integral over [a,b]. Also a continuous scalar function on a compact coordinate box is integrable against the finite Lebesgue measure restricted to that box (or the corresponding finite product measure). Finite measures are s-finite; ℝ with its usual norm is a complete real normed vector space.

grounds.reason: g is smooth, so its coordinate derivative is continuous.
The inserted derivative is continuous and the interval has endpoints −R<R.
R is finite positive and Q has finite volume.
Coordinate measures are standard Lebesgue measures, with the dimension-zero singleton convention.

background_notes.justification: Continuity on a compact set gives a finite uniform bound and Borel measurability; the absolute integral is bounded by that bound times the finite measure. Closed and half-open intervals differ only by endpoints of zero Lebesgue measure, and positive orientation preserves sign. A finite measure is already one finite summand in an s-finite decomposition. Completeness here is the usual completeness of real numbers, which implies convergence of real Cauchy sequences in the absolute-value norm.

background_notes.fact: For n≥1 and 1≤j≤n, iota gives a measure-preserving bijection from Qrest×[−R,R], with the product of restricted coordinate Lebesgue measures, onto Q=[−R,R]^n with restricted Lebesgue measure. Consequently integrals of integrable scalar functions agree under this identification. For n=1 the first factor is the measure-one singleton.

grounds.reason: Lebesgue measures have the specified coordinate-product normalization, including dimension zero.
n≥1 and the fixed j is a valid coordinate.
iota inserts r at j and preserves the original order of all other coordinates.
The domains are the closed coordinate boxes Qrest and Q, with finite restricted measures.

background_notes.justification: iota is a continuous coordinate permutation with continuous inverse on these product spaces. The pushforward product measure and restricted box measure agree on coordinate rectangles because both assign the product of the same coordinate lengths. Both are finite measures; uniqueness from the generating rectangle algebra gives equality on Borel sets. Completion extends the equality to Lebesgue measurable sets. The corresponding integral identity follows first for indicators and simple functions and then for integrable functions. The singleton factor contributes the multiplicative factor one when n=1. This justifies the author's displayed coordinate identification, without replacing the FTC/Fubini route.

background_notes.fact: If a,b,d are real absolutely integrable functions on ℝ^n, d=a+b, and all vanish outside C⊂Q, then ∫_Q d=0 implies ∫_{ℝ^n}a=−∫_{ℝ^n}b. Interchanging the two vectors in the Euclidean dot product leaves a unchanged.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies the derivative identity, support in C and absolute integrability for d=∂_{x_j}g and its two summands.
The Fubini/FTC computation proves the box integral of d is zero.
The dot product is the standard finite-dimensional real Euclidean one.

background_notes.justification: Vanishing outside Q makes whole-space and restricted-box integrals equal. Linearity for integrable real functions gives 0=∫d=∫a+∫b, whence the displayed conclusion by real algebra. Symmetry follows termwise from commutativity of multiplication in the finite coordinate sum defining the real dot product.

background_notes.fact: For smooth g:ℝ^n→ℝ and the coordinate insertion iota defined in S002, r↦g(iota(y,r)) is smooth and has derivative ∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) at every r∈ℝ for every fixed y∈ℝ^(n−1).

grounds.reason: F001 establishes global smoothness of g.
iota fixes all other coordinates and varies the j-th coordinate with slope one.
The dimension is positive and j is a valid coordinate.

background_notes.justification: The insertion map is affine. The chain rule computes its composition derivative by pairing the differential of g with the j-th coordinate vector, which is exactly ∂_{x_j}g. Iterating this fact preserves smoothness; no boundary exception occurs because the line function is defined on all of ℝ.
